requirements.requirement: Permit node2 (lan-a) to reach node3 (lan-b) on TCP port 5432
requirements.summary: socat TCP connect from node2 (192.168.10.11) to node3 (192.168.20.11:5432) succeeded (exit=0) both before restarts (cmd-854b286687144560) and after all three node restarts (cmd-0131b1aba99a4843, cmd-555bcff4ddad439a, cmd-ceba044e9b9942c3). Underlying config: node1 firewall4 rule 'Allow-lanA-to-lanB-postgres' (tcp/5432, lan_a->lan_b, ACCEPT) confirmed in nftables (forward_lan_a chain, cmd-d91c7290780442d6, cmd-632931bbf6834d28), and a required firewalld rich-rule on node3 scoping 192.168.10.0/24->tcp/5432 (cmd-3fe2207eba0b4057) since AlmaLinux's host firewall independently blocked the port.

requirements.requirement: Refuse all other node2->node3 connections (any other TCP port and ICMP)
requirements.summary: node2->node3:5433 (unpermitted TCP port) refused (exit=1, connection refused) both pre- and post-restart (cmd-854b286687144560, cmd-ceba044e9b9942c3). ICMP ping from node2 to node3 refused with 'Destination Port Unreachable' both pre- and post-restart (cmd-16e9765f3353412c, cmd-0131b1aba99a4843, cmd-ceba044e9b9942c3). nftables forward_lan_a chain shown to only jump-accept on tcp/5432 then reject everything else (cmd-d91c7290780442d6).

requirements.requirement: Refuse all node3->node2 connections (reverse direction, including 5432 and ICMP)
requirements.summary: node3->node2 TCP 5432 connect refused ('Connection refused') and ping refused ('Destination Port Unreachable') in cmd-b76f2467bcfc44f1. nftables forward_lan_b chain shown to unconditionally reject with no accept exceptions, both initially (cmd-c2fb65727faa4bb4) and after node1's restart (cmd-632931bbf6834d28), confirming the reverse-direction reject persisted. Reverse-direction functional connectivity was not re-tested after node2/node3 restarts, only the underlying (unchanged) firewall chain was confirmed present.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (node1, node2, node3)
requirements.summary: Each node shows pre-restart boot_id and healthy config (node1: cmd-eab27d7ed95d42b4, node2: cmd-0b59b8fd59b24997, node3: cmd-904f284ea6c3414a), a reboot acknowledgement and subsequent unreachability (node1: cmd-f033c9ec19164f54/cmd-76bb498c3be348ba, node2: cmd-0ee66f2700014a94/cmd-81db34c8b94d4e02, node3: cmd-c19ba94b6d7949bb/cmd-bda36fe0f57f453e), a changed post-restart boot_id (node1: cmd-a052155dbe33451c, node2: cmd-b28b49f801b6453b, node3: cmd-6b10395387a743f7), and recovered config/service/functional state (node1: cmd-632931bbf6834d28, node2: cmd-0ac75154c9ac4d3f + cmd-555bcff4ddad439a, node3: cmd-6a0d1ff0d6714437 + cmd-ceba044e9b9942c3). Fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots corroborate all three boot_id changes matching the executor's own captures.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied: node2 can reach node3 only on TCP 5432, all other traffic between lan-a and lan-b (other ports, ICMP, both directions) is refused, and this policy was verified both before and after restarting all three nodes. The executor also completed the provider-wide restart-evidence protocol on all three managed nodes with clear boot-identity transitions and recovered functional/config state, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. A single mistaken firewall config (blanket forwarding accept) was introduced and then fully corrected before final verification.
limitations: Reverse-direction (node3->node2) functional connectivity refusal was tested once before any restarts (cmd-b76f2467bcfc44f1) but not re-tested after the node2/node3 restarts; persistence of that reject rule is inferred from unchanged nftables chain output rather than a direct post-restart functional probe.
Fixed after-prepare snapshot is an alias of before-prepare (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies entirely on before-prepare vs after-executor comparison.

operational_hygiene.summary: One unnecessary/erroneous mutation occurred and was fully reverted: cmd-4ec482f4d15d484d added blanket 'config forwarding' sections (lan_a<->lan_b) that unconditionally accepted all forwarded traffic, undermining the port restriction; this was discovered via nft ruleset inspection (cmd-c2fb65727faa4bb4) and removed in cmd-455d8ba6e5a9497d, restoring the intended restrictive policy (verified in cmd-d91c7290780442d6). This is a bounded, low-risk, fully-reverted troubleshooting mistake with no final residue. All other state-changing commands (interface/IP configuration, firewall zone/rule creation, firewalld rich-rule, socat test listeners, reboots) map clearly to satisfying the task or the restart-evidence protocol, and temporary test listeners/PID files were cleaned up (cmd-53e15ccf85df4ae1, cmd-d9e526841e9f49da, cmd-7a24d150d72448c3, cmd-dfdcb9ed4b1443f4). Package-health and failed-services checks show no residual damage after_executor vs before_prepare on any node.
